events.text:
—❗️🇮🇷 NEW: The first handwritten note by the Supreme Leader of Iran, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, has been released to the public
It is dated August 1st, 2026, addressed to IRGC Aerospace Commander Brigadier General Majid Mousavi, and confirms that Seyyed Mojtaba is in active correspondence with all relevant authorities and military officials.
The text is as follows:
‘In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
To the brave and Mujahid brother, Brigadier General Seyyed Majid Mousavi—may God protect and support him.
After greetings and salutations:
1). Praise be to God: The report you submitted—a copy of which I had already received—is heartening and gratifying. You have written very little about your own efforts and those of your unsung, self-sacrificing comrades; such is one of the characteristic behaviors of the pious ones.
The outcome—by Divine Wisdom—stemming from this quality is, God willing, affection and esteem that the Almighty (Glory be to Him and Exalted be He) bestows upon the sincere, along with manifold blessings and manifest victories.
2). Regarding the [ballistic missile] supply chain, I hope efforts continue and that reports on the matter are conveyed to me on a regular basis.
3). Safeguarding your own precious life and the lives of all the brothers is my emphatic request. I hope that, through the blessed prayers of our Master (may God hasten his noble reappearance), all affairs will be set right.’

events.text:
Drone near US missile base? Military calls 112
An unauthorized civilian drone was detected near the US Aegis Ashore missile defense base in Redzikowo, Poland, prompting the military to call the national 112 emergency number, Onet reported.
Poland’s Ministry of National Defence stated that the drone remained approximately 1 km from the base, was monitored by military air defense systems, and never approached sensitive facilities or posed a threat. The operator’s location was subsequently identified and reported to the police.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia trapped by geography, making military options against Houthis unviable
Saudi Arabia is facing a zugzwang, with the Houthis advancing while regional alliances struggle to meet Riyadh’s security needs, the Jerusalem Post reports, suggesting a possible Saudi-Israeli rapprochement.
Riyadh has sought air-defense assistance from France, the UK, and Egypt, as well as military support from Turkey and Pakistan under the Mecca Pact.
Israeli officials have highlighted the gap between Saudi Arabia’s needs and the assistance it is actually receiving, arguing that Israel could offer military expertise in countering Ansar Allah, the report says.
But Israel itself has struggled to fend off combined barrages of drones and missiles launched by the Houthis, Hezbollah, and Iran.
Saudi Arabia’s geography leaves its oil infrastructure, the backbone of its economy, vulnerable to attacks from Axis of Resistance forces surrounding the kingdom, political scientist Jean-Francois Seznec argues. Diplomacy backed by China may offer a more viable way forward, he notes, stressing Beijing’s role in restoring Saudi-Iranian relations in 2023.
China’s influence, technological capabilities, and “real leverage in Tehran,” Seznec argues, could give Beijing greater clout in the Gulf than the US (or Israel) possesses.
